description: A Stremio add-on manifest plus the ether block. This schema mirrors the rules enforced by internal/plugins Manifest.Validate; the Go validator is authoritative.

contributes.description: Per-capability metadata. Mandatory metadata is enforced by the Go validator.

events.description: Event subscriptions and custom events published to Ether's event bus. At least one of subscribe or publish is required when events capability is declared.

flowActions.description: Custom actions contributed to Ether Flows (requires flow_actions capability).

uploadPaths.description: Adapter subpath globs that accept uploads streamed to disk. The smallest matching maxBytes applies to the entire wire body.

search.description: Opt a stream_source plugin in to category searches (GET /ether/search). Ether routes an indexer_search with a category only to source plugins that declared one of the requested Newznab categories; a top category (3000) covers its subcategories (3010, 3040). Answers use the stream route's shape: lazy releases are listed on GET /ether/files/{id} and opened on GET /ether/open/{id}?file=&fileIndex=; the bytes stream as a Range source on the plugin's permissions.network hosts.

lookups.description: Typed lookups the plugin answers (for example album or book); a caller's lookup fields reach the plugin as lookup.<field> query parameters.

ai.description: Use the owner's configured language model for bounded completions in actions, jobs, sync, and other non-viewer routes ("complete"), or also on interactive search routes — Stremio catalog search, kinds search, and frontend adapter search routes — with a hard 20 s bound and per-query caching ("complete+search"). Every other viewer/client path stays refused.

media.description: Probe container metadata ({durationSec, container, width, height, sizeBytes}) for a PlayableSource via media.probe from jobs, actions, background sync, and other non-viewer routes ("probe"). Reuses Ether's durable release_probes cache, is rate-limited per plugin, and is bounded at 10 s per probe. Every viewer or client request path is refused.

sources.description: Ask Ether to search indexers and inspect or acquire debrid/Usenet releases via sources.resolve ("search", "search+check", "acquire", or "acquire+check"). The "+check" variants also permit background usenet_check calls in jobs and schedules within the owner's per-plugin daily allowance. Requires the kind_resolver capability.

storage.description: Keep up to 1 GiB of durable blobs per plugin. Durable blobs are removed by cache.delete or plugin uninstall.

limits.description: Hosted/data requests are clamped to owner-controlled global or per-plugin ceilings. Default ceilings: 2 GiB memory (up to wasm32 4 GiB), 12h, effectively unlimited background compute, 8 GiB download/member and 32 GiB total expansion. Viewer request-path time/compute budgets stay tight.

archiveExpandedBytes.description: Clamped to the owner ceiling; omitted or zero uses that ceiling.

archiveMemberBytes.description: Clamped to the owner ceiling; omitted or zero uses that ceiling.

archiveMembers.description: Clamped to the owner ceiling; omitted or zero uses that ceiling.

deadline.description: Positive Go duration; omitted uses the owner ceiling (default 12h).

fetchBytes.description: Clamped to the owner ceiling; omitted or zero uses that ceiling.

maxItems.description: Maximum stored items across the plugin's content libraries; clamped to the owner ceiling unless overridden per plugin.

poolSize.description: Hosted WASM instance pool size; default 2, clamped to the owner ceiling (default 4, raisable up to 16). With poolSize >= 3 at least one instance is reserved exclusively for playback resolves and background jobs hold at most poolSize - 2; with poolSize == 2 background jobs and frontend adapters share at most one instance so resolves and health checks keep one free.

strings.description: Locale to file path or inline key map. en is required when $t: keys are used.

summary.description: Plain text or a $t: key. Sentence case, no em dashes.

id.description: Reverse-DNS, lower case, unique, never reused.
